record.original_question: Characterize those Frobenius varieties whose associated trees satisfy the Bras-Amoros-type growth property that each level has more vertices than the preceding level.

evidence.quote: Another interesting question would be characterizing those Frobenius varieties that verify the Bras-Amoros' conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}_0$. The elements of $\mathbb{N}_0 \setminus S$ are called the gaps of $S$, and the genus $g(S)$ is the number of gaps. Let $n_g$ denote the number of numerical semigroups of genus $g$. The Bras-Amorós conjecture asserts the strict monotonicity $n_{g+1} > n_g$ for all $g \geq 0$.

A Frobenius variety is a nonempty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups satisfying:
(i) if $S, T \in \mathcal{V}$, then $S \cap T \in \mathcal{V}$;
(ii) if $S \in \mathcal{V}$ and $S \neq \mathbb{N}_0$, then $S \cup \{F(S)\} \in \mathcal{V}$, where $F(S)$ denotes the Frobenius number of $S$ (the largest gap).

To any Frobenius variety $\mathcal{V}$ one associates a rooted tree $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{V})$ whose vertices are the elements of $\mathcal{V}$, whose root is $\mathbb{N}_0$, and in which the parent of $S \in \mathcal{V} \setminus \{\mathbb{N}_0\}$ is $S \cup \{F(S)\}$. The level of a vertex $S$ is its distance to the root, equivalently its genus relative to the root. Let $N_h(\mathcal{V})$ denote the number of vertices of $\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{V})$ at level $h$.

Problem. Characterize the Frobenius varieties $\mathcal{V}$ that satisfy the Bras-Amorós-type growth property
$$N_{h+1}(\mathcal{V}) > N_h(\mathcal{V}) \qquad \text{for every } h \geq 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not return any source providing a characterization of Frobenius varieties whose associated tree satisfies the Bras-Amorós-type level-growth condition. The classical Bras-Amorós conjecture (for the full tree of all numerical semigroups) was itself recently announced as proved by Zhai-type asymptotic refinements, but the analogous question for general Frobenius varieties does not appear to have a published characterization. Current status is therefore inconclusive from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Frobenius restricted varieties in numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Frobenius varieties and pseudo-varieties were defined to describe the common behavior of many families of numerical semigroups; the tree structure within them is studied.
status_evidence.claim: Trees associated to Frobenius (restricted) varieties are an active object of study, but no characterization of those satisfying the Bras-Amorós growth property is provided.

status_evidence.title: Maria Bras-Amorós's research works
status_evidence.snippet: Infinite chains of numerical semigroups in the semigroup tree were introduced by Bras-Amorós and Bulygin (2009); computational results show that these chains are rare.
status_evidence.claim: Work on the semigroup tree is ongoing, but the level-growth question for arbitrary Frobenius varieties is not addressed in available references.
